author.name: William Shakespeare
author.biography: Shakespeare left Stratford-upon-Avon for a career in London's theatres, where he worked as an actor, playwright and company shareholder. He knew stories as things people performed before other people, with attention, sympathy and judgment changing from moment to moment. Shakespeare wrote for a society in which marriage joined households as well as individuals. He made a feud's public language collide with the private language two young people invent for themselves.

hook.text: Would you trust a love powerful enough to overturn your whole life?

paragraphs: Romeo and Juliet meet in a world that already has a place for each of them. Their families are enemies. Other people have plans for their futures. Their attraction makes those arrangements suddenly seem unreal.

The play gives young love extraordinary verbal energy. The lovers can make a shared world in a few lines. Outside that world, friends joke, parents negotiate and insults demand a response. Private hope depends on events neither lover can command.

Shakespeare announces tragedy at the beginning, so knowledge of the outcome does not remove the suspense. We watch how often another possibility appears, and how speed, pride and miscommunication can close it. The adults are not simply absent; they are present in ways that often fail to recognise the urgency in front of them.
Listen to the different kinds of language people use to claim authority over love. What could help a powerful feeling survive contact with the world?

orientation.text: The opening chorus tells you the story is tragic. Follow how timing and messages shape what happens, rather than reading only to discover the ending.
